points.label: Creation setting
points.left: The first spoken command is followed by appearance, evaluation, separation, naming, evening, and morning.
points.right: The first-day command becomes a remembered pattern for another kind of illumination.

points.label: Parties, action, or promise
points.left: Speech · seeing · separating · naming · Light · darkness · Darkness-only scene → day/night distinction · Light and darkness distinguished
points.right: Genesis light command echoed · Light · darkness · Cosmic light language → inward illumination · Original event · later metaphorical use

payload.posture: Paul explicitly echoes the creation command when describing illumination in human hearts.
payload.tension: Genesis narrates light entering the created order; Paul reuses that speech for inward knowledge without identifying the two events.
payload.title: Light spoken / light in hearts
